is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on 'immature stages of Anopheles gambiae' (Title).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the presence of 'two kdr mutations L1014S (77%) and L1014F (23%)' (Page 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype frequencies (77% L1014S, 23% L1014F) are provided as descriptive characteristics of the colonies, citing Machani et al. 2020 [21], without associated sample sizes (N) or raw counts for the genotyping in this specific study.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses the 6th generation (F6) of a resistant colony and the 13th generation (F13) of a susceptible colony (Page 2), which exceeds the F1 limit for field populations.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating the fitness costs of insecticide resistance on larval life-traits.

sub_country_location.evidence: The colonies were originally 'collected from Bungoma in western Kenya' (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The paper does not state the years in which the original field collections in Bungoma took place.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The genotype frequencies and colony characterization are explicitly cited from a previous study: 'The two kdr mutations L1014S (77%) and L1014F (23%) were present... [21]', where [21] is Machani et al. 2020.

supplement.evidence: Additional file 1 is mentioned as containing mortality data (Fig S1), but not the required genotype counts.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the fitness costs (larval development and survival) associated with pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.s. from western Kenya. It compares a deltamethrin-selected resistant colony (F6) and a susceptible colony (F13) derived from the same genetic background in Bungoma. While the paper mentions frequencies for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and L995S (kdr-east), these are descriptive of the colonies and cited from Machani et al. (2020) without providing new extractable genotype counts or sample sizes. Additionally, the use of advanced generation colonies (F6/F13) excludes it from the field population requirement.
exclusion_reasons: The study uses laboratory-colonized mosquitoes (F6 and F13 generations) rather than field-caught (F0) or F1 mosquitoes.
Genotype frequencies for Vgsc L995F and L995S are provided without sample sizes (N) or raw counts, and are cited from a previous study (Machani et al. 2020).
